title: The Physical Cost of Context: Quality-Constrained Resource Accounting for Coding Agents
trick: Count the prefill tokens the server actually recomputes, not the tokens sent: masking old observations every turn cut prompt tokens 33% but rewrote the cached prefix, so recomputed prefill rose sevenfold and GPU energy 2.3x.
framing_stripped: Called 'a quality-gated physical-accounting protocol' for 'resource-aware context management'; it is a four-arm, one-device measurement (vLLM or SGLang prefix cache, one request in flight, server counters for uncached prefill, KV bytes-times-seconds, wall time and idle-subtracted nvidia-smi power) of four fixed context policies for coding agents, with a prespecified 5-point non-inferiority gate on task quality applied before any cost is compared (sec. 2.1, 2.4, 3).
method_equations: Executed input work (eq. 1): $$T_{\mathrm{prompt}}(p)=\sum_{t=1}^{n_p}\ell_{p,t},\qquad T_{\mathrm{uncached}}(p)=T_{\mathrm{prompt}}(p)-\sum_{t=1}^{n_p}h_{p,t}=T_{\mathrm{prompt}}(p)-T_{\mathrm{hit}}(p),$$ where $p$ is a context policy, $n_p$ the number of model requests the agent makes under $p$, $\ell_{p,t}$ the logical prompt tokens of request $t$ (what the client sends), $h_{p,t}$ the tokens of request $t$ served from the runtime's longest cached prefix, and $T_{\mathrm{hit}}$ the total reused tokens; for a treatment-minus-control contrast $\Delta T_{\mathrm{uncached}}=\Delta T_{\mathrm{prompt}}-\Delta T_{\mathrm{hit}}$, so a prompt saving raises executed prefill when the policy loses more reusable tokens than it removes (sec. 2.1). Policy algebra (eqs. 2-4): an arm is $p=(\sigma,e,r)$ with scaffold $\sigma\in\{\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{patch}\}$, pre-first-turn evidence $e\in\{\varnothing,R_{10}\}$ ($R_{10}$ = ten dense-retrieved code blocks from the frozen CodeNib index $M_E$ for query $q$), and serialization operator $r$; the visible state is $V^{(e)}_{\sigma,t}=q\oplus e\oplus H_{\sigma,t}$ with $H_{\sigma,t}=(a_1,o_1,\ldots,a_t,o_t)$ the action-observation history and $\oplus$ concatenation, and the model input is $P^{(e,r)}_{\sigma,t}=S_\sigma\oplus r(V^{(e)}_{\sigma,t})$ with $S_\sigma$ the system prompt. Operators: identity $I(V)=V$; anchored compaction $A_\sigma(V^{(R_{10})}_{\sigma,t})=V^{(R_{10})}_{\sigma,t}$ for $t<\tau$ and $D_{\tau,\sigma}\oplus H_{\sigma,\tau+1:t}$ for $t\geq\tau$, where $\tau$ is the first successful source read and $D_{\tau,\sigma}$ a short anchor (query once, the successful read, a bounded assessment) that replaces the candidate list and exploratory history once; masking $L_5(V^{(R_{10})}_{\mathrm{patch},t})=q\oplus R_{10}\oplus H_{\mathrm{patch},t}[o_i\leftarrow\mu(|o_i|)\ \text{for}\ i\leq t-5]$, where $\mu(|o_i|)$ is a line-count placeholder, so every request after the window fills rewrites an observation the previous request sent (sec. 2.3). Arms: Grep $G=(\mathrm{loc},\varnothing,I)$, Mini $N=(\mathrm{patch},\varnothing,I)$, Eager $E_\sigma=(\sigma,R_{10},I)$, Compact $C_\sigma=(\sigma,R_{10},A_\sigma)$, Mask-5 $M_5=(\mathrm{patch},R_{10},L_5)$. Resource vector (eq. 5): $\mathbf{R}(p)=(T_{\mathrm{prompt}},T_{\mathrm{output}},N_{\mathrm{req}},T_{\mathrm{uncached}},L_{\mathrm{TTFT}},L_{\mathrm{wall}},K_{\int},K_{\max},U_{\max},E_{\mathrm{gpu}})$: prompt and output tokens, requests, uncached-prefill tokens, time to first token, wall time, KV time-area $K_{\int}$ (allocated KV bytes integrated over wall time, GiB$\cdot$s), peak KV, peak unified-memory pressure, GPU energy. Quality gate (eq. 6): policy $p$ with control $c(p)$ and quality endpoint $Q$ (answer-block Recall@5 for localization, official resolved rate for patching) is eligible only if $$\operatorname{LCB}_{.95}[Q(p)-Q(c(p))]>-\epsilon,\qquad \epsilon=0.05,$$ with $\operatorname{LCB}_{.95}$ the lower end of a paired 95% interval from a 10,000-draw bootstrap resampling whole repositories; failed tasks stay in every denominator (sec. 2.4). Energy proxy (eq. 7): $E_{\mathrm{raw}}=\sum_i\frac{P_i+P_{i+1}}{2}(t_{i+1}-t_i)$ over 1-second nvidia-smi power samples $(t_i,P_i)$, and $E_{\mathrm{proxy}}=E_{\mathrm{raw}}-\bar P_{\mathrm{idle}}\Delta t$ with $\bar P_{\mathrm{idle}}$ the pre-run mean idle draw and $\Delta t$ the run duration (App. A). Masking break-even (sec. 5, C2): with $\rho$ the fraction of the observed hit tokens a runtime would serve in both arms, Mask-5 changes uncached prefill by $-75.1\mathrm{k}+135.9\mathrm{k}\cdot\rho$ tokens per attempt, which turns positive above $\rho\approx0.55$; at $\rho=0$ (no prefix cache) masking saves prefill.
load_bearing_assumption: That the serving runtime's longest-cached-prefix reuse is the cost model of deployment, so reused tokens are near-free and uncached prefill is the executed work, and that the hit fraction measured here (one request in flight, a dedicated cache reset only per policy-shard block, 'Cached prefixes serve about 96% of Eager's prompt but 53% of Mask-5's', sec. 4.3) carries to real serving. By the paper's own first-order estimate the masking penalty is $-75.1\mathrm{k}+135.9\mathrm{k}\cdot\rho$ and vanishes below $\rho\approx0.55$; under batching or cache pressure that evicts prefixes, which the paper lists as untested, the +608.5% shrinks and can change sign (sec. 5, sec. 7).
weakest_component: The headline number is one window on one arm under ideal caching, with cache loss and trajectory change bundled. (1) Mask-5 is a single fixed policy (SWE-agent's LastNObservations, $n=5$) on top of the preloaded-evidence arm, one trajectory per instance on 100 SWE-bench Verified tasks under a 32-call cap, physical intervals over eight shards; the native-agent-plus-masking cell was not run, and the paper says 'We test four fixed policies; Mask-5 fixes the window at five observations' and 'Window sweeps, LLM summarization, learned pruning, and external memory remain unmeasured' (sec. 7). (2) The +608.5% uncached prefill mixes two effects the paper cannot separate: lost reuse at a fixed token sequence, and the different trajectory masking induces (+2.6% calls, 40 vs 44 submissions); the authors write 'The prefill inversion is consistent with reduced prefix-cache reuse after repeated history edits. Trajectory changes may also contribute to the observed resource differences' (sec. 4.3), and the replay that would split them (Eager's trajectory re-serialized under $L_5$, a deterministic function needing no model) is absent. (3) Serving is single-tenant: 'Results cover two stacks on one DGX Spark serving one request at a time; batching, cache pressure, and cloud GPUs remain untested' (sec. 7), so $\rho$ sits at its ceiling and the result is an upper bound on the masking penalty; 'Peak-KV and system-memory changes are too noisy to support a capacity claim' (sec. 4.2). (4) The localization quality gate and the localization costs come from disjoint cohorts: 'Quality and detailed cost come from different localization cohorts (450 and 100 tasks), so no single issue set carries both measurements' (sec. 7); 'Server, KV, and energy intervals use only three shards' (sec. 7); and 'The instrumented study lacked prospective power analysis' (sec. 3). (5) The gate itself is under-powered for the patch study: a $-3.0$-point difference on $n=100$ fails at $\epsilon=5$ because its lower bound is $-8.6$, so a policy that is in fact non-inferior by 3 points is excluded for lack of sample, and the 'misses the quality gate' headline is partly a sample-size statement. (6) The anchor result reverses the authors' own prior: CodeNib (2607.25431, same group) reported that retiring the candidates after the first source read resolved the most issues of five policies on 200 SWE-bench Verified tasks; here Compact resolves 30 vs Eager 29 vs Mini 30 of 100 under a 32-call cap and 'adds no saving beyond Eager' (sec. 5), without the paper reconciling the two.
regime: Localization: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 (35B total, 3B active) on vLLM, temperature 0, 65,536-token context cap, one measured request at a time, prefix caching off in the resource matrix and toggled in the cache study; 16-turn limit; host NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10 SoC, 128 GB coherent unified memory). Resource cohort: 100 codenib-synthesis tasks over 25 pinned repository snapshots (five each of Python, Go, Rust, TypeScript/JavaScript, C/C++), three repetitions, 900 cells; endpoint answer-block Recall@5 (.470 Grep, .478 Eager, .494 Compact on the quality cohort); prompt 136.8k/90.5k/98.2k tokens per attempt, 13.02/8.38/9.49 successful server calls, 2.007/1.340/1.466 kJ GPU proxy (Table 1). Quality cohort: 450 Python issues from distinct SWE-rebench V2 repositories, one run per policy (1,350 cells), powered for a 441-case requirement. Cache study: same 100 tasks, 600 cells, one vLLM flag toggled: Eager prompt +8.3% (95% CI $[-5.7,+24.7]$), uncached prefill $-67.7$% ($[-71.0,-63.8]$). Patch study: Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 on SGLang RadixAttention with DFlash speculative decoding (eight draft tokens), mini-SWE-agent v2.4.6 with its official prompt, 100 SWE-bench Verified instances over all 12 Python repositories, one trajectory per arm, 32-call and 1,800-second caps, Radix cache reset per policy-shard block, eight shards; resolved 30/29/30/26 of 100 (Mini/Eager/Compact/Mask-5), about 26 calls per attempt, prompt 220.7k/225.6k/210.8k/150.5k, uncached 9.8k/10.0k/12.2k/70.8k, KV frac$\cdot$s 2.94/3.25/2.69/3.55, GPU proxy 1.833/1.956/1.917/4.412 kJ (Table 2). Measured device-hours: 14.11 primary, 4.23 exploratory, 7.90 cache study, 14.65 external patch study (App. A). Energy per wall time stays in 27.7-29.3 W (primary) and 25.2-26.0 W (SGLang), so in the localization study 'energy mainly tracks duration' (sec. 4.2). Code and artifacts: github.com/sysevol-ai/CodeNib.
information_asymmetry: (1) Reporting stage vs server stage: the field's context-management papers report logical prompt tokens, what the client sent, while the executed quantities (uncached prefill, hit tokens, KV time-area) exist on the serving runtime's counters (SGLang's hit/miss counters, vLLM's prefix-cache statistics) and never reach a results table; the paper reads them for four fixed policies on one device and says itself that 'Window sweeps, LLM summarization, learned pruning, and external memory remain unmeasured, although Equation (1) applies to each' (sec. 7), so the executed-prefill column for every published policy in the lane (observation masking at other windows, summarization, SWE-Pruner, memory) is computable from released trajectories and absent. (2) Policy decision vs cache state: $L_5$ rewrites observation $o_{t-5}$ on every request without seeing whether the prefix it breaks is resident; the break-even $-75.1\mathrm{k}+135.9\mathrm{k}\cdot\rho$ depends on $\rho$, a runtime quantity (residency under batching and eviction) the policy does not observe, and per-request hit status is on the server at decision time; CADOC and TokenPilot act on this gap by scheduling edits in batches or by forecast, and the paper runs neither as an arm. (3) Trajectory vs cache attribution: the +608.5% is a mixture of lost reuse at a fixed token sequence and the trajectory change masking induces; both counterfactuals are computable without a model (re-serialize Eager's recorded trajectory under $L_5$ and count longest-common-prefix tokens; re-serialize Mask-5's trajectory under $I$), which is what TurnCost's re-scoring tool does on public trajectories under alternative caching policies, and the paper leaves it: 'Trajectory changes may also contribute to the observed resource differences' (sec. 4.3) and 'traces do not label call intent, so this attribution remains open' (sec. 4.1). (4) Single-request vs concurrent serving (the CL-W43-12 question): $K_{\int}$ is measured with one request in flight, so KV residency never binds and the paper declines a capacity claim ('Peak-KV and system-memory changes are too noisy to support a capacity claim', sec. 4.2); what it supplies is the per-session demand input, KV GiB$\cdot$s per task and the fact that Mask-5 raises KV time-area 9.4% while cutting prompt volume 33.3%, and Compact lowers it 17.2% (Table 2); the binding question lives under batching and cache pressure, which are 'untested' (sec. 7). (5) Price vs physics: the killed probe C-W43-22 and CADOC price the same inversion in cached-input dollars at a provider's cache-read weight; this paper measures it in server-counted tokens, wall seconds and idle-subtracted joules on a local device with no price ratio, which is the price-independent version of the sign the W43 kill record said was already in print; the two accountings coincide only when the price ratio tracks the compute ratio, and neither paper checks that. (6) Quality cohort vs cost cohort: for localization the per-success cost divides a 100-task cost by a 100-task full-recall rate while the gate is passed on 450 other cases, so the per-task joint distribution of quality and cost, which a cost-per-success ruler needs, is missing ('no single issue set carries both measurements', sec. 7).
occupies: Published, with code and artifacts: the decomposition of executed prefill into logical prompt minus reused prefix ($T_{\mathrm{uncached}}=T_{\mathrm{prompt}}-T_{\mathrm{hit}}$) with KV time-area, wall time and an idle-subtracted GPU-energy proxy, gated by a prespecified 5-point non-inferiority test, as a protocol for comparing context policies on a local serving stack; and four results under it: preloading ten retrieved blocks passes the gate and cuts calls 35.7% and the energy proxy 33.2% against grep on 900 localization cells (saving comes from fewer calls, not shorter ones); anchored compaction passes the gate but saves nothing beyond preloading (+13.3% calls); a same-model prefix-cache toggle leaves prompt volume unchanged (+8.3%, CI spans zero) and cuts uncached prefill 67.7%; and SWE-agent's LastNObservations ($n=5$) with mini-SWE-agent on 100 SWE-bench Verified instances cuts prompt volume 33.3% while losing 135.9k reusable tokens per task, raising uncached prefill 608.5%, wall time 36.9% and the energy proxy 125.6%, with 26 vs 29 resolved and a failed gate, plus the first-order break-even $\rho\approx0.55$. Beyond CADOC (2609.37012), which per its abstract schedules object-to-Card replacements in batches by balancing accumulated waiting cost against shared cache-reconstruction cost and reports about 40% lower input cost, and which per the W43 kill record of C-W43-22 states the trim-versus-keep break-even and replays SWE-bench histories at several cache-read price weights: this paper adds (a) the measurement in physical units read off server counters and a power meter rather than price-weighted tokens, so the sign of the inversion does not depend on a provider's cache discount; (b) a prespecified quality gate that the masking policy fails, making the cost comparison conditional on quality; (c) the same-model cache on/off isolation of the reuse term; (d) the negative result on the field's reference masking policy in an unmodified external scaffold with official grading; and (e) the separation of evidence delivery from history retention as the lever that saves (calls) versus the one that multiplies (edits). It does not occupy: dollar pricing or re-pricing of published results (TurnCost, CADOC); batched, multi-tenant or cloud serving; window sweeps; summarization, learned pruning or external-memory arms; batched-edit policies (CADOC, TokenPilot) as arms; or the trajectory-versus-cache decomposition of its own headline.

neighbors.title: CADOC: Cache-Aware Dynamic Object Context for Long-Horizon Agents
neighbors.trick: Replace structured objects in the history with short retrievable Cards, but commit the replacements in batches sized by an economic-order-quantity trade-off between waiting cost and the shared cost of rebuilding the broken prefix cache, cutting input cost about 40% at near-full-context quality; this card's paper measures the same inversion in server-counted prefill and joules instead of priced tokens, and runs no batched-edit arm.

neighbors.title: The Complexity Trap: Simple Observation Masking Is as Efficient as LLM Summarization for Agent Context Management
neighbors.trick: Drop old environment observations from SWE-agent's context instead of summarizing them and find it halves cost against the raw agent at a matching solve rate across five model configurations; this card's paper takes the same LastNObservations operator and reports it multiplies uncached prefill sevenfold and fails a quality gate once prefix reuse is counted.

neighbors.title: TokenPilot: Cache-Efficient Context Management for LLM Agents
neighbors.trick: Stabilize the prompt prefix at the ingestion gate and evict expired context segments only on a conservative batch-turn schedule, so pruning does not shift the layout and invalidate the prompt cache, reporting 56-87% cost cuts on PinchBench and Claw-Eval; the engineered fix for the penalty this card's paper measures, not run as an arm here.

neighbors.title: TurnCost: Turns, Not Observations: Cache-Aware Loop Engineering for Coding Agents
neighbors.trick: Re-score 600 public coding-agent trajectories under cache-aware pricing and find 98.6% of input tokens are served from a prefix cache, that turn count explains 84% of the variance in log cost against 4% for observation size, and release a tool for re-scoring corpora under alternative caching and pricing; the released-trajectory, price-side counterpart of this card's measured-device accounting, and the tool that could split this card's trajectory and cache effects.

neighbors.title: CodeNib: A Multi-View Data System for Serving Repository Context to Coding Agents
neighbors.trick: Compile lexical, dense and structural views of one commit behind one manifest so an agent's reused context can be checked against a rebuild or a live server, and report that handing the agent candidates and retiring them after its first source read resolves the most SWE-bench Verified issues of five policies; the same group's index and the origin of the Eager and Compact arms whose anchor saves nothing further in this card's paper.

theme_fit.why: executed prefill, KV time-area, wall time and GPU energy of an agentic workload under prefix-cache reuse, with the reuse term isolated by a same-model cache toggle; the lane sentence's 'true cost structure of agentic workloads' and 'prefix and KV-cache reuse' directly, and a new neighbour of CL-W43-12 and of the killed C-W43-22
two lossy context edits (anchored compaction, observation masking) measured for what they cost under a quality gate in a controlled four-arm comparison; measurement register, no new recipe
supplies a ruler: a prespecified non-inferiority gate before cost comparison, failures charged in every denominator, cost per successful endpoint; the gate's power at n=100 is itself an L1 question
serving-only; no training, credit or RL

limitations_as_complaints: My 608.5% masking penalty was measured with one request in flight on one DGX Spark, where the cache is never evicted between calls, so my hit fraction is at its ceiling and by my own formula ($-75.1\mathrm{k}+135.9\mathrm{k}\cdot\rho$) the penalty shrinks or reverses under batching or cache pressure; I have not run that: 'Results cover two stacks on one DGX Spark serving one request at a time; batching, cache pressure, and cloud GPUs remain untested.' (sec. 7)

I tested one masking window and one anchor, both fixed, so I cannot say what the executed-prefill column looks like for the policies the field actually ships: 'We test four fixed policies; Mask-5 fixes the window at five observations, following the SWE-agent reference. Window sweeps, LLM summarization, learned pruning, and external memory remain unmeasured, although Equation (1) applies to each.' (sec. 7)

I cannot say how much of the masking penalty is lost cache reuse and how much is the different trajectory masking induces, because my traces do not label why the agent made each extra call: 'The prefill inversion is consistent with reduced prefix-cache reuse after repeated history edits. Trajectory changes may also contribute to the observed resource differences.' (sec. 4.3) and 'traces do not label call intent, so this attribution remains open.' (sec. 4.1)
